_documentation: Hand-curated controlled vocabulary for the directory's research-interest keywords. Several sections drive the same surface. `acronyms` is a flat list of preferred display forms (UN, NATO, EU, IoT, …); when one of those words appears anywhere in a submitted keyword, the sync emits it in the canonical form rather than letting the sentence-case normaliser mangle it. `proper_nouns` works identically but for capitalised place names (countries and regions): the sentence-case normaliser only capitalises the first word of a keyword, so without this list a mid-phrase Afghanistan or Ukraine would render lowercased (`Russia-ukraine war`). Both lists are matched case-insensitively against each token and emitted in the exact form listed here, so keep each entry in its correct display form. Because the match is per token, a place name of two or more words (Latin America, Middle East) cannot live here and goes in `aliases` instead, where the lookup is on the whole keyword. `aliases` maps a canonical display form to a list of lowercased aliases that resolve to it; use this when two genuinely-distinct submitted phrases should collapse (e.g. `fpa` → `Foreign policy analysis`, or `political economy of europe` → `Political economy`). scripts/sync-bios.py reads this file, normalises each bio's `keywords` into a `canonical_keywords` field, and logs Levenshtein-close pairs that aren't already merged so the maintainer can decide whether to add them. A `spelling` section is a word-level map from American to British spellings (lowercased key → lowercased British form); during the word-walk each letter-run matching a key is rewritten to its British form before sentence-casing, so `Defense` becomes `Defence` and `Cyber defense` becomes `Cyber defence`. It deliberately omits `program`, which is valid British English in the computing sense. Two hygiene behaviours run in the normaliser itself (not this file): a standalone `&` between words becomes `and` (R&D and other &-bearing acronyms are matched whole and untouched), and a non-fatal warning is printed for any canonical keyword over 40 characters or containing parentheses, so phrase-like submissions get curated into a tighter tag or an alias here rather than shipping as a singleton. A `themes` section groups canonical keywords under a small set of broad research themes; the sync derives a per-bio `themes` array plus a top-level `theme_aggregate` (distinct-member count per theme) and `keyword_theme_map`, which drive the directory's research-theme filter chips while member cards keep their specific keyword pills. A canonical keyword with no theme listed here is logged non-fatally at sync time so the taxonomy stays complete. An `affiliation_aliases` section maps a canonical institution name to a list of spelling variants that should fold into it; the sync applies it inside normalise_affiliation after punctuation normalisation, so one employer renders one way across the directory. Punctuation normalisation alone cannot merge differently-worded names for the same place (`ETH Center for Security Studies` vs `ETH Zurich, Center for Security Studies`), so this hand-curated map is the only mechanism that does. A `regions` section is a flat controlled vocabulary of research-region display names (modelled on the EU Institute for Security Studies' regions); the sync matches the Research-regions form cell case-insensitively against it, emits a per-bio `regions` array plus a top-level `region_aggregate`, and drives the directory's research-region filter (a second axis, independent of the topical themes). The file is hand-edited; changes land in the same PR that submits the new bio (or in a periodic curation pass). `drop_keywords` lists country and sub-region names typed into the keyword box: the regions facet owns geography and `regions` only holds the eight broad controlled regions, so a bare "Ireland" or "MENA region" otherwise stood alone in the theme filter meaning nothing. It is matched on the whole canonical form and never on a word inside one, so the themed keyword "India" and the keyword "Russia-Ukraine war" both survive. It also holds a submitted keyword retired by a curation pass (Post structural security, #1831). `splits` maps a submitted phrase to the several canonical keywords it actually names, for an entry that is a sentence rather than a tag: aliasing cannot help there, since an alias maps many forms onto one and this needs the opposite.

Promotions so far: domestic political change reached its 4-member threshold in July 2026 and became `Democracy, governance and political change`. `Climate, energy and environmental security` was added in August 2026 at 2 members, below that threshold, as a deliberate maintainer decision (#1701) rather than a cluster promotion, on the grounds that an Action about European security with no environmental theme is a gap a reader notices whatever the member count says. It stands at 4 members in September 2026, Energy security having sat under it since it was created. `War, military history and armed conflict` was promoted in September 2026 on reaching the 4-member threshold (Bennett, Morgan-Owen, Karlén, Zhao), carving seven keywords out of Security and defence, which goes from 39 members to 38. Promoting a theme needs its FR and DE labels added to assets/js/site.js in the same PR, because the fifteenth theme shipped untranslated and rendered in English on both filter rows.
